demos.blurb: Ranked across every country in the world — computed, not looked up.

state.q: Which countries cut child mortality the fastest since 2000?
state.answer: Maldives cut under-5 mortality 86.3% between 2000 and 2024 — from 39.5 to 5.4 deaths per 1,000 live births — the steepest fall of any country. All ten leaders more than halved their rate, with China and Sao Tome and Principe close behind.

demos.question: Does higher health spending buy lower child mortality?
demos.blurb: A correlation across every reporting country, one point each — computed live.

state.q: Does higher health spending buy lower child mortality?
state.answer: Across 190 countries in 2023 the correlation between health spending per person and under-5 mortality is -0.45 — modest and negative. On a log spending scale it strengthens to -0.76, which is the shape talking: mortality falls steeply over the first few hundred dollars per person and then flattens, so the countries with the most to gain are the ones spending least.

demos.question: Have the G7 actually decoupled CO₂ from economic growth?
demos.blurb: Joins Our World in Data emissions with World Bank income — two databases, one chart.

state.q: Have the G7 actually decoupled CO₂ from economic growth?
state.answer: Yes, and by a wide margin: across the G7 average, output per person reached 148 by 2024 against a 1990 base of 100, while CO₂ per person fell to 66. The two lines separate in the mid-2000s and never reconverge — growth and territorial emissions genuinely came apart.
